title: He Asked for a 56,000-Rupee PC
desc:
In the 1990s Rahul Sharma asked his father for a computer that cost about 56,000 rupees. With no internet at home, he learned from books and started a business.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Micromax Started With Phone Booths
desc:
Before its own phones, Micromax made wireless booth phones that ran on a SIM card for India's yellow STD-PCO booths.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: The Phone With a 30-Day Battery
desc:
Power cuts in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar gave Rahul the idea: a phone whose battery could last up to 30 days on standby. The 2008 Micromax X1i.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: No Shop Would Stock It
desc:
Distributors said customers only ask for Nokia. One old distributor tried it, and the first batch of about 10,000 phones sold out in around 10 days.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: One Customer, Then None
desc:
Micromax's booth phones had one big customer. Then, as the founders tell it, that customer walked away, and Micromax went straight to the phone companies.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: The Ad Before Karva Chauth
desc:
A stylish phone for women barely sold. Then came a TV ad with Akshay Kumar and Twinkle Khanna, right before Karva Chauth.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Half the Price of a Samsung
desc:
Big screens, dual SIMs and big batteries at half the price. Small-town India loved Micromax's Canvas phones.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Branded in India, Built in China
desc:
By 2014 Micromax was on top in India. But most of its phones were designed with, and built by, partners in China.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: The Indian Brand That Beat Samsung
desc:
In 2014 an Indian phone brand outsold Samsung in India. Five years later it had almost no market left.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Four Friends, One IT Company
desc:
In 2000 Rahul Sharma, Vikas Jain, Rajesh Agarwal and Sumeet Kumar set up Micromax as a small IT company.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Suspect 1: The Chinese Brands
desc:
Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo arrived with flash sales, huge ad budgets, fat margins for shopkeepers, and phones they built themselves.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Suspect 2: Jio
desc:
On 5 September 2016 Reliance Jio launched with free calls and free 4G data. Overnight India wanted 4G phones, and Micromax had warehouses of 3G stock.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Suspect 3: Micromax Itself
desc:
Slow to switch, spread across tablets and TVs, and without its own technology, Micromax couldn't get 4G chips as quickly as global rivals.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: The 'In' Comeback
desc:
In 2020, after the India-China border clash, Micromax tried a comeback with its 'In' brand. It got headlines, not market share.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: The Verdict: Who Killed Micromax?
desc:
Jio pulled the trigger, Chinese rivals were waiting, and Micromax was built on other people's technology. The lesson for every Indian start-up.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.
